buildings.description:
Publishes the human guide, browsable pattern library, package references, and
generated agent documentation used to apply JSKIT consistently.
buildings.name: guidance
buildings.publicContract:
Readers can browse the documentation site or consume the distributed agent-docs
package. Human guide sources define architectural meaning; the documented build
generates packaged references and pattern projections. Generated outputs must
remain reproducible from their authored sources.
buildings.title: Framework guidance and patterns

buildings.description:
Provides the capability, feature, action, HTTP, storage, realtime, and mobile
runtime primitives from which applications assemble their own behavior.
buildings.name: application-runtime
buildings.publicContract:
Applications import explicit npm entry points and compose named capabilities,
providers, actions, and runtime adapters. Long-running work and application
policy remain owned by the consuming application. Missing requirements fail at
composition or at the relevant operation boundary rather than being resolved
through a global service locator.
buildings.title: Application runtime composition

buildings.description:
Provides conversation runtimes, provider selection, voice support, reusable
connector account management, and focused third-party operations.
buildings.name: assistant-and-integrations
buildings.publicContract:
Applications select supported assistant and connector providers, retain their
own conversation and connection identities, and supply credentials through
server-side environment references. Conversations preserve provider lifecycle,
streaming, attachment, recovery, and storage contracts. Connector operations
remain scoped to the application and user or workspace that owns the account.
buildings.title: Assistants and external integrations

buildings.description:
Provides reusable database, resource, CRUD, JSON API, upload, and transactional
payment or reward mechanics while leaving schemas and product workflows with
their owning package or application.
buildings.name: data-and-resources
buildings.publicContract:
Consumers select a supported database driver, discover package-owned immutable
migrations, and use explicit repositories and transactions. Resource operations
provide validated read and mutation contracts, predictable missing-record and
failure behavior, and application-supplied authorization context. Upload,
payment, and reward facilities require application-owned configuration and
storage; selecting a package does not provision an external service.
buildings.title: Data and resource operations

buildings.description:
Provides authentication-neutral identity contracts plus local and Supabase
providers, account profiles, authenticated web routes, and workspace tenancy.
buildings.name: identity-and-workspaces
buildings.publicContract:
Applications choose and configure an authentication provider, associate its
verified identity with existing application users, and authorize account and
workspace operations through explicit features and routes. Managed Preview can
exchange a host-authorized selector for an existing development user's normal
application session; it neither creates users nor grants roles.
buildings.title: Identity, users, and workspaces

buildings.description:
Provides Vue components, composables, shell placements, responsive resource
screens, authenticated account and workspace surfaces, billing, uploads, and
shared action feedback.
buildings.name: web-experiences
buildings.publicContract:
Applications compose public exports and placements into their own routes and
themes. Standard resource screens expose loading, empty, error, permission,
filtering, navigation, and mutation states through shared composables. The
application remains responsible for route policy, product vocabulary, and the
server authorization behind every visible action.
buildings.title: Web application experiences

buildings.description:
Coordinates workspace checks, generated documentation and catalogue artifacts,
and the versioned publication of all public JSKIT packages.
buildings.name: repository-lifecycle
buildings.publicContract:
`npm run verify` is the local aggregate check for lint, release contracts,
runtime dependency boundaries, CI declarations, package metadata, generated
artifacts, and workspace tests. Release preparation increments the coordinated
package cohort and regenerates tracked artifacts for review. Publication accepts
only a clean, current `main` checkout and publishes packages in dependency order;
registry verification is a separate network-dependent operation.
buildings.title: Repository verification and release

buildings.description:
Provides the published JSKIT package catalogue, package-graph validation,
shared ESLint presets, and workspace test helpers.
buildings.name: catalogue
buildings.publicContract:
The `jskit` executable checks or updates an application's coordinated JSKIT
package graph using published catalogue metadata. Repository validation checks
package metadata and dependency rules. Shared lint and test exports give JSKIT
packages and consumers consistent development conventions without generating
application source.
buildings.title: Package catalogue and development tooling

districts.description:
Owns the published JSKIT libraries, application patterns, package migrations,
browser-facing components, server runtimes, and the human and distributed agent
documentation. Packages expose explicit npm entry points so applications can
compose only the capabilities they need.
districts.title: Framework packages

districts.description:
Owns the package catalogue, package-graph checks, shared lint configuration,
and test helpers used to develop and release the workspace.
districts.title: Developer tooling

districts.description:
Owns workspace-level verification, generated-artifact checks, coordinated npm
release preparation and publication, and continuous-integration orchestration.
The more specific package and tooling directories retain ownership of their own
implementation.
districts.title: Repository operations
